text: dsh-plugin-codemode（DSH 插件，客户端信息未在已读代码中声明）：为 DSH 提供 Code Mode 工具，让模型编写 JavaScript 脚本，在沙箱中一次编排多次宿主工具调用。它把工具列表和说明桥接到脚本环境，支持并发调用、按需查询工具帮助，并可将日志与返回值汇总后截断输出。执行可选 V8 VM 或 QuickJS，并可配置 worker 隔离、执行时限和顶层工具白名单。适合需要批量检索、读取多个文件或筛选工具结果的 DSH 工作流。安装入口为 dsh plugin add；代码没有要求额外账户或 API key。

dsh-plugin-codemode adds a Code Mode tool to DSH. JavaScript scripts run in a sandbox, discover and concurrently call host tools, then return processed results. It supports V8 or QuickJS, optional worker isolation, timeouts, and output limits. Install with `dsh plugin add`.

dsh-plugin-codemode 的功能「脚本工具编排」：模型通过 codemode 工具提交 JavaScript，脚本可调用已注册的 DSH 工具并处理结果。输入为脚本，输出为执行日志和显式返回值。
dsh-plugin-codemode 的功能「工具发现与帮助」：脚本可获取当前可见工具名称，并按名称或描述查询工具参数说明；通过工具脚本调用时触发。
dsh-plugin-codemode 的功能「并发工具调用」：脚本可并行调用工具，桥接器最多同时执行 16 个调用，超出的调用进入等待队列。
dsh-plugin-codemode 的功能「执行结果整理」：运行结束后格式化状态、日志和返回值，并将整体输出限制在配置的字符上限内。
我想减少多轮逐个调用工具的过程，一次完成查询和整理。

**Pi-style Code Mode (Programmatic Tool Calling) for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**  
Turn verbose O(N) multi-turn ReAct loops into a single O(1) JavaScript orchestration script executed in a memory-isolated sandbox — see [Security Model](#-security-model) for what that does and does **not** guarantee.

---

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ⚡ The Benchmark: Hard Numbers：**Measured 2026-10-15** against the **17 real markdown documents** in the *DeepSeekHarness* repository's `docs/` folder (including the 282,842-char operational ledger `known-issues.md`) — **414,346 raw characters** in total. The task: scan all documents, filter by keywords (`JEV`, `Polymarket`, `Architecture`), extract titles & line metrics, and return a sorted Top-5 summary JSON.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ⚡ The Benchmark: Hard Numbers：| Metric | Traditional ReAct Loop | Code Mode (Sandbox Orchestration) | Measured Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Data Loaded into Context** | 414,346 chars | **677 chars** | **99.8% Reduction** (612:1 distillation) |
| **Estimated Input Tokens** | ~129,483 tokens | **~212 tokens** | **99.8% Saved** (129k tokens spared) |
| **Agent / LLM Turns** | 19 round trips | **1 turn** | **94.7% Fewer Turns** (18 turns eliminated) |
| **End-to-End Elapsed Time** | ~47.5 s (at 2.5s / LLM turn) | **~2.5 s** | **19× Faster** (94.7% latency drop) |
| **Computation Accuracy** | Prone to LLM counting hallucinations | Native JS `Array.filter().sort()` | **100% Deterministic & Accurate** |

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ⚡ The Benchmark: Hard Numbers：> ⚠ **The absolute figures are a dated snapshot, not a constant.** The corpus keeps growing — it was **215,011 chars** when this table was first written, and is **414,346** as of 2026-10-15. The *ratios* are the stable part; refresh the absolutes by re-running:
>
> `node <DeepSeekHarness>/tests/benchmark-codemode-vs-react.mjs` — from the **DeepSeekHarness repo root**, because the corpus is **that** repo's `docs/`, not this plugin's (this plugin's own `docs/` holds a single file).
>
> `End-to-End Elapsed Time` is **modelled** (19 turns × 2.5 s/turn assumed), not stopwatch-measured.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 💡 Why Code Mode?：Modern LLM agents suffer from tool explosion and context pollution:
1. **Context Bloat**: Reading 20 files fills the transcript with 200k tokens of raw data. The model loses track, forgets system instructions, or triggers expensive context compaction.
2. **High Latency**: Every single tool call requires a full round trip of network latency and model inference.
3. **Calculation Flaws**: Asking LLMs to count lines, sort arrays, or calculate statistics over huge text chunks often yields subtle hallucinations.
dsh-plugin-codemode README · The Code Mode Paradigm：> *"Put deterministic things in code, non-deterministic in LLM."* — Hacker News Community Consensus on Code Mode

dsh-plugin-codemode README · The Code Mode Paradigm：Inspired by **Pi 1.0 (Earendil)**'s Code Mode architecture and Cloudflare's production agent rewrite:
- **[Pi.dev 1.0 Official Codemode Docs](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/codemode)**: Established the Programmatic Tool Calling paradigm via memory-isolated sandboxing and deferred tool exposure.
- **[Cloudflare / CamelAI Case Study](https://x.com/Vercantez/article/2082138839888589200)**: Rewrote agents from heavy VM containers to Pi Code Mode in Durable Objects, reporting an order-of-magnitude reduction in latency and token costs.
- **Hacker News Discussion ([#49019301](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49019301))**: Highlighted that orchestrating multi-tool workflows via local sandboxed code delivers up to a **99.2% cost reduction** compared to traditional ReAct loops.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · The Code Mode Paradigm：With Code Mode, the agent writes a concise JavaScript async function. The script executes inside an isolated sandbox, concurrently calls registered host and MCP tools, filters out unnecessary data in memory, and **only returns the final distilled result** to the conversation context.

---

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ✨ Features：- **🚀 Dual-Engine Execution**:
  - **V8 VM Engine (`engine: 'vm'`, Default)**: Aligns with DSH's official PTC workflow architecture. Zero overhead, handles multi-megabyte payloads, native microsecond performance.
  - **QuickJS-WASM Engine (`engine: 'quickjs'`)**: Strict WebAssembly memory isolation, zero Node/OS footprint.
- **🔄 Universal Tool Proxy & Dynamic Introspection**:
  - Access all DSH built-in tools (`read`, `edit`, `pwsh`, `glob`) and MCP tools (`mcp__github__*`, `mcp__cua*`, `mcp__tavily__*`) via `tools.<tool_name>(args)`.
  - **Zero-Token Tool Discovery**: Introspect tools dynamically at runtime without polluting system prompts or wasting context tokens:
    - `tools.list()`: Returns the full array of registered tool names in memory.
    - `tools.help('namePattern')`: Inspects parameters and JSON Schemas on-demand inside the sandbox, cutting system prompt bloat by over 90%.
- **🛡 Hard-Safety Protections**:
  - **Hard timeout** (default 60,000 ms). The host channel yields a macrotask and re-checks the
    deadline on every tool call, so `await`-driven infinite loops are **terminated** instead of
    starving the event loop. Pure s

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🔐 Security Model：**The sandbox executes model-generated code. Treat that code as untrusted** — prompt injection
can reach it through any tool result or file it reads.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · What is enforced：| Guarantee | Engine | How |
|---|---|---|
| No host object crosses into the sandbox | `vm`, `quickjs` | The host exposes exactly one channel and it carries **strings only**; the sandbox-side `tools` proxy and its `JSON.parse` are built *inside* the context |
| Sandbox global has no host prototype | `vm` | `vm.createContext(Object.create(null))` — a plain literal's prototype is the **host** `Object.prototype`, which handed `globalThis.constructor` straight to the host `Function` constructor |
| Tool return values cannot be an escape channel | `vm`, `quickjs` | Values are serialized on the host and re-parsed by the **sandbox's own** `JSON` |
| `await`-driven infinite loops terminate | `vm` | The host channel yields a macrotask and re-checks a deadline on every call |
| Synchronous infinite loops terminate | `vm` | V8 `runInContext({ timeout })` |
| **Any** infinite loop terminates, including a pure `await` loop that never calls a tool | `vm` + `hardIsolation: true` | The sandbox runs in a **worker thread**, so the host's event loop stays free and `worker.terminate()` always fires. Without this flag the host and the sandbox share one even

dsh-plugin-codemode README · What is **not** guaranteed：- **`node:vm` is not a security boundary.** Node's own documentation states:
  *"The `node:vm` module is not a security mechanism. Do not use it to run untrusted code."*
  The hardening above closes **10 known prototype-chain vectors** (pinned by `test/escape.test.js`),
  but a `vm` context still shares the host process and heap. It is a **defense-in-depth** measure,
  not a boundary. For a real boundary, run the whole DSH process inside a container or a separate
  OS user.
- **`hardIsolation` defaults to `false`.** With it off, a script that loops on `await` without ever
  calling a tool starves the shared event loop and hangs the DSH process until it is restarted.
  Set `hardIsolation: true` in the profile config if you want that class closed.
- **No network isolation.** The sandbox has no `fetch` because none is injected — a convenience
  property, not an enforced capability.
- **No approval gate.** Every tool call the script makes executes immediately; DSH's own approval
  surface is not consulted by codemode.
- **The `quickjs` engine is slower.** It is an interpreter (roughly 10–50× slower than V8 JIT per
  the comparison

dsh-plugin-codemode README · Option A: `dsh plugin add` (Recommended)：```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-codemode
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml`), so the host row is inserted
into your profile automatically — nothing to hand-edit. Restart DSH and the `codemode`
tool appears.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · Option B: Install from npm manually：In your DSH profile directory (e.g. `~/.dsh/profiles/web`):
```bash
pnpm add dsh-plugin-codemode
section: Option B: Install from npm manually

dsh-plugin-codemode README · or: npm install dsh-plugin-codemode：```

Then add the row yourself to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:
```yaml
- insert:
    - id: plugin-codemode
      name: 'dsh-plugin-codemode'
      config:                  # 全部可选;省略即用默认值
        toolName: 'codemode'
        engine: 'vm'           # 'vm' (default) or 'quickjs'
        maxResultChars: 50000
        timeoutMs: 60000
        injectGuidance: true
```

git clone https://github.com/Yum-wu/dsh-plugin-codemode.git
cd dsh-plugin-codemode
npm install
npm run build

Link into your DSH web profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`):

dsh-plugin-codemode README · Restart DSH：Restart the DSH service from your desktop management console. The agent will immediately receive the `codemode` tool declaration and execution guidance.

---

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ⚙️ Configuration Reference：| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `toolName` | `string` | `'codemode'` | Name of the tool declared to the LLM. |
| `engine` | `'vm' \| 'quickjs'` | `'vm'` | Execution engine: high-throughput V8 VM or WASM sandbox. |
| `hardIsolation` | `boolean` | `false` | Run the sandbox in a **worker thread** and kill it with `worker.terminate()`. Closes the one remaining hang class (a pure `await` loop that never calls a tool) and turns WASM-level crashes into clean failures. Costs one worker spawn per call. **Recommended for untrusted input** — see [Security Model](#-security-model). |
| `maxResultChars` | `number` | `50000` | Maximum length of distilled output returned to context. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `60000` | Hard deadline per script before auto-termination. |
| `injectGuidance` | `boolean` | `true` | Injects Code Mode orchestration tips into system prompt. |
| `collapseTopLevelTools` | `boolean` | `false` | When on, **only whitelisted tools stay visible at the top level**; the rest vanish from the model’s view. |
| `allowedTopLevelTools` | `string[]` | `DEFAULT_CORE_TOOLS` (37 items) | The whitelist

dsh-plugin-codemode README · ⚙️ Configuration Reference：> ⚠️ **`allowedTopLevelTools` REPLACES the default, it does not extend it.** The implementation is `new Set(config.allowedTopLevelTools || DEFAULT_CORE_TOOLS)` — once you set this array, `DEFAULT_CORE_TOOLS` is **ignored entirely**.
> Tools you leave out **disappear from the top level silently**: no error, no warning, nothing in the logs. The model simply cannot see them.
> Measured 2026-10-05: the old `DEFAULT_CORE_TOOLS` had only 11 entries while the runtime registered 36 non-MCP tools — 24 were swallowed, `subagent` among them. Now completed to 37 entries with a guard test. |

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧠 Auto Reasoning Effort — moved out (2026-10-05)：This plugin no longer implements reasoning-effort selection. It now lives in a standalone
plugin: **[dsh-auto-reasoning](https://github.com/Yum-wu/dsh-auto-reasoning)**.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧠 Auto Reasoning Effort — moved out (2026-10-05)：**Why it moved.** The old code here mounted the platform hook `agent/request`, read
`agent/session` + `session/event`, called `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo()` and registered a
host `/api` route — **not one line of it belonged to codemode's sandbox / tool-bridge /
truncator.** The hook position was right; the plugin identity was wrong.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧠 Auto Reasoning Effort — moved out (2026-10-05)：**How the two are wired now.** The declaration row for `dsh-auto-reasoning` is shipped by the
**dsh-jev-preset** bundle (same insert group, second row), so installing the JEV preset brings
auto effort with it. codemode is not involved either way.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧠 Auto Reasoning Effort — moved out (2026-10-05)：> ⚠️ **Remove `autoReasoning: true` from your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.** The config key no
> longer exists, and cordis validates a whole entry at once — a leftover unknown key makes the
> entire `plugin-codemode` entry fail to activate, which shows up as *"the codemode tool
> vanished"*.

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧠 Auto Reasoning Effort — moved out (2026-10-05)：> ⚠️ **Do not add `auto: auto` to a model's `reasoningEfforts`.** That advice used to live in this
> README and it is **wrong**: `auto` is not a legal effort key (the legal set is
> `off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max`), and declaring it there makes the whole provider
> entry fail to activate — every model under it disappears from the picker. Verified against a
> real profile on 2026-10-04; a guard test now ships in DeepSeekHarness
> (`tests/11-cordis-efforts-schema.test.mjs`).

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🛟 3-Level Zero-Risk Rollback Strategy：| Level | Scenario | Action | Recovery Time | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Level 1 (Soft Disable)** | Unstable model behavior | Add `disabled: true` to `plugin-codemode` in `cordis.patch.yml` and restart DSH. | < 15 seconds | Unregisters `codemode`, reverts to standard single-turn tools. |
| **Level 2 (Runtime Fallback)** | Script syntax or runtime error | Automatic: plugin catches errors and prompts model to fallback to native step-by-step tools. | 0 seconds (instant) | Session is never interrupted; graceful degradation. |
| **Level 3 (Physical Clean)** | Complete uninstall | Remove from `cordis.patch.yml` and `package.json`, delete directory. | < 15 seconds | 0 runtime traces, 0 configuration residues. |

dsh-plugin-codemode README · 🧪 Testing：```bash
npm test
```
Runs the unit suite (**37 cases**, `node --test test/*.test.js`):
- `sandbox.test.js` (4): basic evaluation and return values, `console.log`/`text()` capture, isolation (no Node process/filesystem leaks), hard timeout on infinite loops.
- `bridge.test.js` (3): `Promise.all` parallel tool execution, rejection of recursive `codemode` calls, oversized-output truncation.
